newsitem.title: FRANCE: French MATIF to shut potato futures on May 27.
newsitem.headline: French MATIF to shut potato futures on May 27.

text.p: French exchange MATIF will shut down trading in potato futures on May 27, the expiry day for the sole remaining May contract, a spokeswoman said.
The decision to close the 13-year-old Paris contract, which originated in Lille, stems mainly from declining volume and was taken after talks with the industry, she said.
Previously quoted contracts for next November and February had been suspended in February, with no open interest.
On Friday, May had an open position of 149 20-tonne lots.

After feverish trading in 1994, volume has declined steadily. The spokeswoman said this seemed linked to the small number of operators, most of them thinly capitalised, and a drop in the importance of the 50-mm Bintje variety quoted on MATIF.
Average daily volume has fallen from 134 lots in 1994 to 20 lots in the first four month sof this year.
MATIF continues to quote wheat, rapeseed and sugar on its commodities floor and is a major market for financial futures.
